name: Nets and folding, 2D to 3D
definition: A net is a flat shape that folds into a solid. The useful question is never what does it look like flat, but which faces end up opposite each other and which edges meet. Tracking one face and its neighbours as you fold is more reliable than imagining the whole thing at once.
recognizeWhen: which of these nets folds into a cube
when the net is folded, which face is opposite
the box is unfolded and laid flat
which pattern would be on the hidden face
misconceptions: I checked that the net had six squares and assumed that was enough.
I tried to picture the whole fold at once instead of tracking one face at a time.
I thought two squares next to each other in the net end up opposite each other.
